verses.verse:
संयुज्या धस्तनाच्छिद्रा दूर्ध्वच्छिद्रं प्रपूर्यते।
तस्मा दधस्तनं मुक्त्वा तत ऊर्ध्व विमोचयेत्।९०।
verses.text: The upper hole is completed by joining with the hole below; therefore, having released the lower one, one should then release the upper.

commentary.text: That is, the note from any hole becomes fully true only when at least two holes below that hole are open and the upper hole gets their proper support. Keeping this in mind, when the practitioner opens the first hole from the bottom, then for its completeness he takes support from the lowest hole, which itself always stays open. So if the lower hole has been closed by some chance object, it must certainly be opened. Now, when you lift the second finger, keep the finger lifted before it raised as well. In the same way, while lifting the third finger, keep the first and second fingers open too. But when you lift the first finger of the other hand, that is, the fourth finger, put the first raised finger back on its hole at the same time. Keep that hole closed until the last, that is, the sixth, hole is open. In this way, up to the last hole, all the holes will keep getting the support of their neighbours too, and the flute will not fall from the hand. Then, coming back, as you close three holes from the top, open the lowest finger, and close all the holes in order from the top.

subsection.title: Practice of the Tongue and of the Fingers
